prompt: A formal, dignified portrait photograph of a revered master, under one warm light: front view, full figure and head-and-shoulders, standing straight and still, evenly exposed. Studio-lit, composed and still, in the manner of a portrait made to honour its subject. Not documentary, not street photography, not reportage, not concept art, not an illustration, not a painting. 9:16 vertical. SUBJECT: a revered master in his sixties - a great sage who was born a king, of the line of Kusika. He carries himself like a man who ruled before he renounced. Build: upright and broad-shouldered, physically strong. Lean from discipline, never gaunt and never starved. He holds his full height. Hair: long grey-white hair gathered and BOUND HIGH AS A CROWN at the top of the head - kept, ordered, dignified, tied close. A long full beard, grey-white, clean and well combed. Complexion: deep warm brown, even and healthy, and NONE LIGHTER. Skin that is looked after: no caking, no powder, nothing applied to it anywhere. His forehead is bare and clean. Dress: a black antelope skin over one shoulder; below it a simple bark-toned lower cloth, clean, deliberately draped and well kept. Clean, dignified, well-kept - never ragged, never torn, never impoverished. No saffron and no orange anywhere. Ornament: almost nothing. No jewellery, no beads across the chest, no pendant, no metal at the throat or wrist. Carries: a plain dark dense-wood staff, shoulder-height, worn pale at the grip, blunt and splayed at the base from years on stone. No carving, no finial. The one thing to get right: his eyes REST on what they look at, and there is authority in them. They do not search, they do not glare, and they do not plead. Must be distinct from VASISHTHA at a glance: hair bound high as a crown against hair combed and tied flat at the crown; a long full beard against a beard cut short; a black antelope skin over the shoulder against the sacred thread on a bare shoulder; bark-toned cloth against undyed white; broad and strong against older and softer. Cloth is woven, cut from the loom, and draped: antariya at the waist, uttariya over the shoulder. Never tailored, never buttoned. Any ornament a character wears comes from the relief vocabulary - Bharhut, Sanchi, Amaravati: heavy kundala earrings that pull the lobe, flat collars and torques, armlets above the bicep, bangles. Gold that gleams, never glitters. No faceted gems. A character whose dress names no ornament wears none. Faces from the real range of the subcontinent. Nose bridges, eye shapes, jaws and cheeks that vary. Pores, oil sheen, sun on skin that has lived outdoors, age in the neck and hands. Bodies are real. No gym physiques. Barefoot on stone. Never sharpen features to read noble or broaden them to read lowly. photoreal, film grain. uncut draped handloom - no stitched garment.

judging_order: THE EYE TEST FIRST, before any particular: would a king rise from his throne to receive this man? If the answer is no, nothing else about the plate matters.
THEN THE FACE. Is this a face that can carry fourteen shots and still be one person? Age in the neck and hands, eyes that rest with authority, no glare, no plea, no beatific smile.
Then the bearing: upright, broad-shouldered, full height. Lean from discipline, not starved.
Then the hair: gathered and bound high as a crown, kept and ordered. Not loose, not wild, and not rope.
Then the skin: deep warm brown, even, none lighter, nothing applied to it, forehead bare.
Then the dress: antelope skin over one shoulder, bark-toned lower cloth, clean and deliberately draped. Nothing ragged.
